verified: Every class named here was confirmed present by querying the installed library with omc. Nothing in this file is written from memory.
how_to_search: Match the task against `keywords` and `use_for`, then narrow by `domains`, which use the Understanding's own domain keys. `reference_models` gives a whole-system pattern from the MSL for a system of that shape; start there when one matches. `rules` applies in every domain.

reference_models.case: two-vessel sequenced transfer with operator commands
reference_models.shape: Two vessels, three discrete valves, a supply boundary and a drain boundary, operator buttons, one controller.
parameterisation: Declare `package Medium = ...` ONCE at model level and put `redeclare package Medium = Medium` on every fluid component. A component left on the default medium will not connect to one that was redeclared.

dp_nominal must be NON-ZERO. Verified by simulation: dp_nominal = 0 fails to build, while omitting portsData or the dynamics setting still simulates. The MSL uses dp_nominal = 1 Pa for a gravity-driven valve between two vessels, and 1e5 Pa for a valve fed from a pressurised supply. Size m_flow_nominal so the open flow matches the rate the brief states.

Give each OpenTank nPorts and one portsData entry per port: the inlet at `height = <tank height>`, the outlet at `height = 0`, each with diameter, zeta_out = 0 and zeta_in = 1. Connect them by index -- tank.ports[1] is the inlet, tank.ports[2] the outlet.
Drive the network with a pressure difference: a supply Boundary_pT well above ambient, and a drain Boundary_pT at `p = system.p_ambient, T = system.T_ambient`.
Read a vessel's level into the controller with `Modelica.Blocks.Sources.RealExpression level1(y = tank1.level)` and connect its `y`. Do not reach into the tank from the controller's own equations.
Set `inner Modelica.Fluid.System system(energyDynamics = Modelica.Fluid.Types.Dynamics.FixedInitial)`, as the MSL example does.

reference_models.case: staged multi-vessel batch plant with evaporation and recycle returns
reference_models.shape: Tanks with top ports, an evaporator/condenser vessel, discrete valves, two return pumps, junction volumes, a sequencing controller.

reference_models.case: quasi-static magnetic circuit with a leakage branch
reference_models.shape: Series iron segments, a split into a useful air gap and a parallel leakage branch, a rejoin, a magnetic ground, and a winding with its own electrical ground and prescribed current.

components.use_for: Integrates a rate into an inventory: total mass, energy, or a species mass.
A PI controller, where the brief states a continuous control law.
components.note: Only when the brief gives the control law and its gains. Do not introduce feedback control a sequenced plant does not have.

components.use_for: A command or permissive arriving at a custom block.
A measurement or setpoint arriving at a custom block.
A threshold with a deadband, where the brief approves one.
components.note: Only when the brief states or approves a deadband. Adding one to settle a threshold silently changes the criterion.

components.use_for: Ramps a Boolean command into a finite-rate signal, such as a pump starting.
Sums two signals, e.g. inflow minus outflow.
Converts a Boolean command into a reportable Real, for the results file.
Scales a signal by a constant, e.g. a net flow into a level rate.
Multiplies two signals, e.g. a mass times a mass fraction.
Clamps a signal to a stated bound.
components.note: Only for a bound the brief states. A limiter added to keep a value plausible hides the discrepancy instead of reporting it.

components.use_for: An operator or command schedule that TOGGLES its output at each listed time.
components.note: It toggles, it does not pulse. Give each momentary command a PAIR of entries {t, t+w}, and make w at least twice the controller scan period or a sampled scan can miss the press entirely.

components.use_for: A multi-column schedule of setpoints or commands over time.
A mutually-exclusive operator button, as the MSL controlled-tank example uses.
A signal that holds, ramps, and holds again.
Exposes an internal value, such as a vessel's level, as a signal for the controller or the results file.
components.note: This is how a controller reads a plant value: RealExpression(y = tank1.level) and connect its y to the controller input, rather than referring to the vessel from the controller's own equations.

components.use_for: A single-column time series of a Real setpoint.
Electrical ground for the winding circuit.
Winding resistance, where the brief gives one.
Reads an induced or terminal voltage.
A current that holds, ramps to a final value over a stated duration, then holds.
components.note: A prescribed excitation profile is a SOURCE, not a state machine: hold-ramp-hold is offset, startTime and duration on one block.

components.use_for: A current source driven by a signal, for an arbitrary prescribed excitation.
A multi-way junction gathering several branches onto one port.
A junction carrying a small volume where several branches meet.
components.note: Required wherever branches meet or can be isolated together: two pressure-drop-only elements connected directly leave the pressure between them undetermined.

components.use_for: A pump whose speed or head is commanded from a signal.
Routing that stores mass and energy, for a line whose own inventory matters.
Routing between units with friction and static head, storing no mass.
components.note: height_ab carries the static head between two elevations; a non-horizontal run without it loses gravity entirely.

components.use_for: Reads mass flow through a two-port sensor.
Reads pressure at a point.
Reads temperature at a point without affecting the flow.
A supply source or receiving drain at fixed pressure and temperature.
A prescribed mass flow into the system.
Global fluid settings. Exactly one `inner Modelica.Fluid.System system;` in the top-level model.
components.note: REQUIRED by every Modelica.Fluid component; each resolves it by name. Without it the model does not elaborate.

components.use_for: A commanded on/off valve taking a Boolean `open` input.
components.note: dp_nominal must be NON-ZERO or the model fails to build -- verified by simulation. The MSL uses 1 Pa for a gravity-driven valve between two vessels and 1e5 Pa for a valve fed from a pressurised supply. Size m_flow_nominal so the flow while open matches the rate the brief states, and record that sizing as an assumption.

components.use_for: An on/off valve that ramps over a finite stroke time instead of switching instantly.
components.note: Use when a datasheet gives stroke times AND the brief requires them modelled; otherwise ValveDiscrete.

components.use_for: A continuously modulated valve with a Real 0..1 opening.
A closed vessel with no free surface.
A vented vessel with a free surface. Renders as a tank with a live level.
components.note: nPorts must equal the number of connections this vessel actually has, with one portsData entry per port, and EACH ports[i] takes exactly ONE connect. A vessel fed from two sources and drained to one needs nPorts = 3. Connecting two components to the same ports[i] is rejected during translation with 'each ports[i] of volume can at most be connected to one component'. Give each entry its diameter and height -- an inlet at height = <tank height>, an outlet at height = 0 -- with zeta_out = 0 and zeta_in = 1. A port above the liquid surface restricts outflow, so port height is hydraulics rather than sizing.

components.use_for: Icon base for the top-level runnable experiment.
A fixed magnetic reluctance, for a gap or segment given directly as R_m.
Couples an electrical winding to the magnetic circuit; the turns count sets the mmf.
Magnetic ground; the reference node of the magnetic circuit.
components.note: A magnetic circuit needs this AND an electrical ground. Omitting either leaves the system structurally singular.

components.use_for: A leakage branch sized by a coefficient relative to the useful flux path.
components.note: Sits in parallel between the split and rejoin nodes so total flux equals useful plus leakage. Series iron must sit BEFORE the split.

components.use_for: Reads the flux in a branch.
An iron segment whose reluctance follows from its geometry and relative permeability.
A commanded mmf source, when the brief drives the circuit magnetically rather than through a winding.
components.note: Prefer the ElectroMagneticConverter when the brief gives a real winding and its turns, since the turns count is then evidence rather than an assumption.

components.use_for: Constant-property liquid water; cheapest choice when no phase change is modelled.
Pure-water medium for a baseline or a topology/control integration check.
components.note: Cannot carry a species mass fraction at all, so it can never satisfy composition-based acceptance.

components.use_for: Entry step of a graphical sequential function chart.
components.note: Graphical sequencing is optional. A custom controller with an enumeration mode is usually safer where freeze/resume or command priority applies.

components.use_for: A StateGraph transition fired by a Boolean signal.
Convective heat transfer, e.g. a cooling coil to a vessel.
Thermal inertia of a mass being heated or cooled.
Conductive heat transfer between two thermal nodes.
Reads the temperature of a thermal node.
A constant-temperature boundary, e.g. cooling water or ambient.
A commanded heat input, such as an electric heater duty.

do.rule: Put exactly one `inner Modelica.Fluid.System system;` in the top-level model whenever any Modelica.Fluid component is used.
do.why: Every Fluid component resolves it by name; without it the model does not elaborate.

do.rule: Declare the medium once at model level and redeclare it on every fluid component.
do.why: A component left on the default medium will not connect to one that was redeclared.

do.rule: Give every valve a non-zero dp_nominal.
do.why: A valve with dp_nominal = 0 fails to build. The MSL uses 1 Pa where flow is gravity-driven between vessels, and 1e5 Pa where the valve is fed from a pressurised supply.
do.evidence: Verified by simulating the same network three ways: dp_nominal = 0 fails, while omitting portsData or the dynamics setting still simulates.

do.rule: Give a vessel one port per connection and connect each port index exactly once.
do.why: A ports[i] carrying two connections is rejected during translation with 'each ports[i] of volume can at most be connected to one component'; the message names no file or line, so it is not repairable by reading it.
do.evidence: The NaCl plant reached the compiler for the first time and failed on exactly this, having reused a port index instead of raising nPorts.

do.rule: Build a plant of named vessels, valves, pumps and boundaries from the acausal library components.
do.why: They carry their own icons, ports and hydraulics, so the diagram, the level dynamics and the port behaviour come for free, and the topology is a connect() graph a reviewer can read.
do.evidence: A two-vessel plant written with a custom tank class per vessel and Real signals compiled and simulated, but rendered as unlabelled rectangles and duplicated the vessel as two near-identical classes.

do.rule: Give every vessel port its elevation through portsData.
do.why: A port above the liquid surface must restrict outflow, so port height changes the hydraulics rather than only the sizing.

do.rule: Put a junction volume wherever branches meet or can be isolated together.
do.why: Two pressure-drop-only elements connected directly leave the pressure between them undetermined.

do.rule: Derive a momentary command's width from the scan period: cmdWidth = 2 * scanPeriod.
do.why: A sampled scan cannot see a press shorter than one scan, and nothing reports the miss.
do.evidence: scanPeriod 0.1 s with 0.05 s presses: a STOP at 220 s was never seen, the controller stayed in its transfer state for 200 s, and the run still looked plausible because a later command happened to land on a scan boundary and did fire.

do.rule: Give each momentary command a PAIR of BooleanTable entries per occurrence.
do.why: BooleanTable toggles at every listed time rather than pulsing, so {t1, t2} yields a single rising edge and silently loses the second command.

do.rule: Model a prescribed input profile as a source block carrying its times and values.
do.why: Hold, ramp, hold is offset, startTime and duration on one Ramp block. It is a signal, not a sequence of states.
do.evidence: A quasi-static magnetic benchmark was given a five-state machine whose guards tested only elapsed time, for a system with no actuators and no operator commands at all.

do.rule: Use a composition-dependent medium when the acceptance criteria are about composition.
do.why: A pure-water medium cannot carry a species mass fraction at all, so it can never satisfy such a check.

do.rule: Place every component and give every connect() a graphical Line annotation.
do.why: The bundle is inspected in OMEdit, and a connection with no annotation cannot be drawn.

do.rule: Report a missing parameter, correlation coefficient or medium property as a gap.
do.why: An invented value is indistinguishable from an evidenced one once it is in the model.

dont.rule: Do not hand-write a tank, valve or pump class when the library has one.
dont.why: A custom class has no icon, no fluid ports and no hydraulics; and a Real signal is not a flow, so nothing enforces mass continuity across the connection.

dont.rule: Do not fall back to the signal-flow form for a plant because it feels more controllable.
dont.why: The warnings attached to that form are the hazards of using it, not evidence that it is the safer choice.

dont.rule: Do not feed a vessel's resulting outflow back into the valve that sets it.
dont.why: That closes an algebraic loop which the solver satisfies with every flow at zero, and the run still reports success.

dont.rule: Do not write a state machine for a system whose only time-varying input is prescribed.
dont.why: A guard testing only elapsed time, with no measured quantity and no command in it, is the signature of a waveform being modelled as a sequence.

dont.rule: Do not write a transition whose source and target are the same state in order to recompute a value.
dont.why: A quantity that varies continuously belongs in an equation, not in a self-transition.

dont.rule: Do not place a series element between the two branch nodes of a parallel magnetic path.
dont.why: Series iron must sit BEFORE the split, or a spurious third parallel path appears and total flux no longer equals useful plus leakage.

dont.rule: Do not omit either ground from a magnetic circuit.
dont.why: Both a magnetic ground and an electrical ground are required; omitting either leaves the system structurally singular.

dont.rule: Do not add epsilon margins, change StopTime, or tune against a reference trajectory.
dont.why: The brief's thresholds and horizon are authoritative, and a recorded run is evidence about the past, never a forcing function.

dont.rule: Do not treat a clean compile as evidence of correctness.
dont.why: A stub with no equation section, a physically wrong parameter, a pulse that fires once and a process stuck in one phase have all compiled and simulated cleanly here.
